subject: Price shelter and rollback-trigger request — KiteHealth (multi-year)
messages:
From: Simon Park <simon.park@kitehealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kayla Mendes <legal@kitehealth.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Price shelter and rollback-trigger: multiyear procurement

Irene —

Thanks again for the demo today. KiteHealth is planning a 36-month commitment across our clinical AI workloads and we need a procurement-ready pricing construct that preserves predictability for our finance team. Two specific asks:

1) A firm multiyear price shelter (price lock) for 24–36 months so our model unit economics remain stable for forecasting.
2) A rollback-trigger clause: if Redwood changes list pricing or materially changes the serving model that increases per-token cost > X% (we can agree on the threshold), we want an automatic rollback mechanism or a credit/escrow that protects our effective unit price for the contract period.

We understand these are non-standard; please escalate to deal desk / execs and let us know what guardrails you need (usage commit, minimum ARR, uplift caps, operational counters). Procurement is aiming to sign before end of Q3; Kayla from legal is cc'd for the contract side.

I've attached a short write-up of our forecast and procurement constraints (KiteHealth_MAAP_request.pdf). Happy to hop on a call if helpful.

Best,
Simon Park
CTO, KiteHealth
Simon.Park@kitehealth.com

Simon —

Appreciate the detail and the timing note. I’m escalating this to our Deal Desk and Sales leadership so we can put forward an executable framework quickly. To make progress this week, could you confirm two items:

- Target committed ARR or minimum yearly spend (ballpark is fine)
- Whether KiteHealth needs a 24- or 36-month guaranteed lock (you mentioned both)

High level on our side: we can consider a combination of (a) a fixed price period (price shelter) + (b) an uplift cap tied to CPI or a fixed % annually + (c) a contractual renewal-protection clause that defines when an automatic remediation (credit or rollback) kicks in. The escrow approach is feasible but will need approval from Deal Desk / Finance and likely a lightweight third-party escrow vehicle.

I’ve looped in Marissa for exec context and Aditya to run Deal Desk feasibility. I’ll consolidate and get back with a proposed term sheet by EOD Tue.

—

Simon / team —

Quick executive note: we can support a multi-year stability package but with firm guardrails. For initial approval, I am comfortable with the following framework to be formalized by Deal Desk:

- Price shelter term: 24 months guaranteed firm pricing (can consider 36 months with minimum ARR commitment)
- Uplift cap: 8% nominal annual uplift maximum (exceptions require CFO sign-off)
- Renewal protection: automatic 60-day notice prior to renewal; if Redwood revises list pricing > 8% in a renewal window, KiteHealth gets either a credit equal to the delta or the option to terminate without penalty within 30 days
- Escrow: acceptable in principle for customer credits/overage protection; Deal Desk to scope escrow provider and operational flow

Aditya — please run final feasibility (Finance, Treasury, legal touchpoints) and surface any constraints or required thresholds (minimum ARR, payment cadence, audit windows). Irene — please ask KiteHealth to confirm the committed ARR band so we can land on 24 vs 36 months.

Marissa
VP, North America Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Simon Park <simon.park@kitehealth.com>
Cc: legal@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 20:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Price shelter and rollback-trigger: multiyear procurement

Team —

Deal Desk + Finance have reviewed Marissa's guidance and can approve with the following conditions for signature-ready language:

1) Final term: 18 months firm price lock (we can extend to 24 months once KiteHealth commits to a minimum ARR of $2.5M/year)
2) Uplift cap: 6% annual cap (fixed %; CPI adjustments not accepted inside the cap)
3) Renewal protection / rollback-trigger: if a price increase > 6% is applied during the contract term, KiteHealth may elect a remediation consisting of either a pro-rata credit to preserve the effective unit price for the remainder of the firm term or the option to transition to a compatible model variant approved by Redwood without penalty; exceptions require CFO approval
4) Escrow mechanics: Deal Desk prefers a third-party escrow holding a pre-funded credit pool equal to 3 months of committed spend; legal to draft an escrow schedule and release triggers
5) Audit & monitoring: KiteHealth to provide monthly usage reporting for the first 12 months and quarterly thereafter; Redwood reserves the right to verify usage with a single audit per year

Irene — I’m attaching the redlined SOW with the above clauses and a DocuSign envelope placeholder. If KiteHealth confirms commitment band, Deal Desk will produce a final term sheet and an updated SOW for signature within 3 business days.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Head of Deal Desk, Redwood Inference
